text: CE-CERT refuse trucks spend more time on urban freeways compared to urban other roads and a very small amount of time on rural freeways. FleetDNA refuse pickup trucks spent the majority of their time on urban other roads and only a small amount on urban freeways. For transit buses, FleetDNA vehicles again spend much more time on urban other roads; FleetDNA vocation is the purple “mass transit” in Figure 53. CE-CERT buses spend much more time on urban freeways, with express buses slightly more on freeways than hybrid buses. 68 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. For FleetDNA and CE-CERT individually, we maintain orange and gray shading for categories of caution and those that are otherwise excluded. Because weekends and weekdays have different shading colors in the data density section, we used whichever shade was more favorable (e.g., if there was a caution on weekdays and an exclusion shade on weekends, we used the orange caution color). Comparing FleetDNA to CE-CERT, we see that they are typically within 10% of each other for time spent on a day type, with variations by each source type. For example, FleetDNA shows less weekday driving for combination-unit short-haul trucks on rural roads and urban freeways and approximately equal proportions on urban other roads. For this source, when there are more data, such as on urban roads, the two data sets are in better agreement.
